scope: Corollary 7.4 of the manuscript “Scalar Potentials and Slow Clocks for Forced Fluid Computation” (preprints/Scalar-Potentials-and-Slow-Clocks-for-Forced-Fluid-Computation-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 82005335f0aac60f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For fixed computable ν > 0, the machine and input effectively determine a smooth prescribed force on [0, ∞) × T3, whose unique global smooth solution from zero velocity and with pressure zero satisfies ∃t ≥ 0 ∃X ∈ S : u3(t, X) > 1/2 ⇐⇒ the machine halts. Uniqueness holds in the torus classical comparison class of Section 2: the velocity, its time derivative and spatial derivatives through order two are continuous on each finite closed cylinder, and the periodic pressure and its gradient are continuous, with mean-zero pressure normalization. No uniform large-time amplitude bound or mean-zero condition is asserted for this force.
